newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares fall, but rebound expected soon.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares fall, but rebound expected soon.

text.p: Polish shares fell for the third consecutive session on Thursday but analysts said the slip, likely caused by profit-taking after 11.6 percent growth since mid-August, was likely to end on Friday or early next week.
The main market's WIG index fell 1.6 percent, to 13,657.4, and turnover fell 22.7 percent to 85.3 million zlotys ($31.1 million) on both markets as 63 issues fell, seven rose and seven were flat.
"The correction should soon end, with the last day of falls possibly tomorrow or Monday, and we are likely to return to the uptrend," said Wojciech Kossuth, a analysts at Bank Slaski.

Analysts said the ruling left-wing coalition crisis, which followed the sacking of foreign trade minister Jacek Buchacz on Wednesday, could slow down the expected growth next week, but was unlikely to stop it, unless the coalition collapsed.
"If the coalition fell apart we could even fall below the 13,000-point support of the WIG index," Kossuth said.
Analysts also said that next week the bourse might be influenced by investors speculating before the release of companies' August earnings reports.
They said they expected the results, due in mid-September, to match July results in being slightly better than those shown in the first half of 1996 and to help keep a good market mood.
None of the stocks in the continuous trade system saw action on Thursday.

Mass privatisation NFI units rose 4.1 percent in soaring 20.6-million zloty ($7.5 million) turnover in the regular session and rose 2.5 percent in 4.0-million-zloty ($1.5 million) continuous trade. Analysts said they were likely to keep growing.
